intro.title: Build online presence tracker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple online presence tracker that monitors whether a user is currently active or idle on a webpage. You will learn how to use event listeners to detect user interactions like mouse movements and key presses. The core programming concept involves managing state to track the user's status and updating it based on real-time events. You'll work with JavaScript's built-in browser APIs, such as setTimeout and clearTimeout, to handle timing logic for determining idle states. This project will help you understand how to create responsive web applications that react to user behavior.
intro.usecase: Online presence trackers are essential in collaborative applications like Slack, Discord, and Google Docs, where they display real-time user status indicators (online/offline/away). Developers implement these systems in customer support dashboards to show agent availability, in project management tools like Trello to indicate active team members, and in multiplayer gaming platforms to show which friends are currently playing. This pattern involves maintaining WebSocket connections, updating user status in databases, and broadcasting presence changes to connected clients—a fundamental skill for building responsive, collaborative web applications.
